## Relic: read the project's documents before reporting
Read these with `file_read` before a finding that depends on what the code is meant to do:
- `AGENTS.md`: the repository map, the architecture rules, the standards and the table of generated code.
- `web/layers/site/content/docs/`: what users are told Relic does. Settings are in `2.installation/6.configuration.md`, features in `3.guides/`, the CLI in `5.cli/`.

Behaviour that one of these documents states as intended is not a defect. Report against it only when the code contradicts the document, and name the document and its section in the finding.

Project facts:
- Go 1.27: `new(expr)`, per-iteration loop variables and `for range n` are valid.
- No code comments is the rule. Never ask for a comment or a docstring beyond the one-sentence doc comment on an exported identifier.
- Generated files are never edited by hand (`AGENTS.md`, "Generated code"). Report the source, not the output.
- Every query exists twice, in `queries/postgresql` and `queries/sqlite`, and every migration in both `migrations/` folders. A difference in behaviour between the two engines is a finding.
- Integration tests carry the `integration` build tag and live in `_integration_test.go` files. A missing test beside the code is not a finding.
- Relic has no production users yet: its own names are renamed outright, with no alias or compatibility shim.

## This file: a Go test
Judge whether the test makes sense, not only whether it is valid Go. Read the code it tests with `file_read` first.
- It asserts behaviour a caller can observe. A test that cannot fail is a finding: one that only checks no error came back where a result matters, repeats the implementation's own computation, or compares a value with itself.
- It would fail if the behaviour its name states broke. When it would not, name the change to the code under test that it misses.
- Its name says what it proves, and each failure message says what was wanted and what was got.
- Inputs that share one shape are table-driven with named cases, and independent tests call `t.Parallel()`.
- An integration test carries `//go:build integration`, gets its database from `databasetest.NewDB` and passes on both engines. A test that calls `databasetest.RequirePostgreSQL` needs a reason only PostgreSQL can give.
- It does not depend on timing (fixed sleeps, one deadline shared by several waits), on test order, on a fixed port or on global state it does not restore.
- Two tests that prove the same thing are a finding, and so is a test whose assertions do not match its name.
The standards are in `AGENTS.md`, "Go" and "Checks before calling work done".

## This file: a web test
Vitest unit tests are in `web/test`, Playwright end-to-end tests in `web/e2e`. Judge whether the test makes sense: it asserts what a user or a caller sees, it would fail if that behaviour broke, and its name says what it proves. An end-to-end test is independent: it creates what it needs under a unique name, finds elements by role or label, waits on conditions and never for a fixed time, and leaves global settings as it found them (`AGENTS.md`, "Web" and "Checks before calling work done").

## This file: a compatibility scenario or its runner
A scenario is a test that drives real clients against a running Relic. Judge whether it makes sense: each step asserts an outcome (a count, a checksum, a status, a message) and does not only run a command; the `# covers:` line lists commands the script really runs; a `# tier:` line gives its reason. A scenario is independent: it uses `$REPO`, `$REPO2` and `$BUILD` from `lib.sh` or names of its own, and leaves global settings as it found them (`AGENTS.md`, "Checks before calling work done").

## This file: the compatibility adapter
Wire field names, status codes, header names and error envelopes in this tree are a contract with existing clients. Do not report them as inconsistent naming, a wrong status or leaked detail. Translation between wire documents and the domain belongs here, and no domain package imports this tree. Fields the domain does not model go under an `extensions` key. Scripts under `compat/` are tests.

## This file: the Relic API in protobuf
Every method declares `option (relic.v1.access)`; an interceptor enforces it and fails closed. File contents never travel in messages: they are plain HTTP under `/api/v1/files/` and `/api/v1/archive/` (`AGENTS.md`, "Architecture rules"). Names follow the Naming standard in `AGENTS.md`.

## This file: SQL
Migrations change the schema only; a data conversion in a migration is a finding. Every query is parameterized. SQLite queries take arrays as JSON for `json_each` and times as fixed-width UTC text, and keep the name, kind, parameters and column order of the PostgreSQL query (`AGENTS.md`, "SQL and migrations", `0017-single-node-backends.md`).

## This file: the web UI
Nuxt 4 with Nuxt UI v4. Backend calls go through `useRelic()` and uploads through `uploadFile`; only the API reference page fetches the OpenAPI document directly. Semantic colour classes only (`text-muted`, `bg-elevated`); a raw palette class is a finding. API messages map to view models in `app/utils/mappers.ts`, and pages stay thin (`AGENTS.md`, "Web"). The session cookie is honoured under `/api/` only, and writes made with it need the `X-Relic-UI` header.

## This file: the chart and the deployment files
The server listens on 8090 and serves metrics on 8091 (`web/layers/site/content/docs/2.installation/6.configuration.md`); the chart's Service stays on port 80. Chart values are described in `web/layers/site/content/docs/2.installation/4.kubernetes/6.values.md`. Dashboards and alert rules are generated by `tools/dashgen` (`AGENTS.md`, "Generated code"). Credentials in the Compose files are development defaults bound to loopback.

## This file: Go
Layering is enforced by depguard (`AGENTS.md`, "Architecture rules"): modules under `internal/` import downwards only, `platform`, `access`, `artifacts`, `scanning`, `delivery`, `app`; packages under `api/` use domain services and never import `internal/platform/database`. Errors wrap with `%w`, map to Connect codes in `api/relicapi/access.go` and never reach a client as internal text. A new operation has a span and metrics whose label values are bounded. Background work runs as River jobs; scanners run as subprocesses.
